Lessons.Title: Writing Inverse Functions to Solve Problems
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: write an inverse for a linear function stated in function notation, use it to solve a contextual problem or reverse a data model, and explain which input/output roles change. Original Edulytiks lesson based on Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 4 Lesson 17, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/4/17/preparation.html and student lesson https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/4/17/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source intentionally delays notation f^(-1) to prioritize meaning; this candidate uses 'inverse process' and does not force that symbol.

Independent tank model: water volume W(t)=80−2.5t litres for elapsed time t minutes until empty, 0≤t≤32. To find elapsed time from a remaining volume v litres, solve v=80−2.5t for t=(80−v)/2.5. Inverse input v is restricted to [0,80] litres and output time lies in [0,32] minutes. W(13)=47.5 litres; if only5 litres remain, t=(80−5)/2.5=30 minutes.

Original second hypothetical data model: a measured-looking percentage indicator increases approximately as P(t)=12+3.5t for years t∈[0,6]. Given an indicator level p, the inverse model t=(p−12)/3.5 estimates the year offset. This is invented for mathematical practice and does not describe actual phone subscriptions or real populations. Extrapolation past observed years may fail.

Student activity: explain inverse operation to a peer, construct forward/backward tables, sketch the input/output interchange, interpret a fractional time estimate and critique when a fitted model is not physically invertible beyond its observed range. Teacher-scored rubric 0–2 each for algebra, checked function composition, valid interpretation of units/domains and responsible modeling limitations.

KeyConcepts.Title: Inverse as reverse question
KeyConcepts.Definition: Given original output, solve for the input that produced it.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Rewrite the output equation and isolate input.

KeyConcepts.Title: Swapped units
KeyConcepts.Definition: Original output units become inverse input units.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Name the quantity when giving a number.

KeyConcepts.Title: Model inversion limits
KeyConcepts.Definition: An inverse algebra formula can produce values beyond a physical or fitted model's domain.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Check output range and original data coverage.
KeyConcepts.Example: Tank cannot have negative volume even if formula evaluated after32min.

WorkedExamples.Title: Find tank water after time
WorkedExamples.Question: Evaluate W(13)=80−2.5×13.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use an original function and check its rule, inverse, constraints, and units at multiple inputs.

WorkedExamples.Title: Find time from remaining water
WorkedExamples.Question: If tank holds 5 litres, how many minutes elapsed?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use an original function and check its rule, inverse, constraints, and units at multiple inputs.
WorkedExamples.Check: Both units and domain t≤32 satisfy.

WorkedExamples.Title: Invert a hypothetical linear trend
WorkedExamples.Question: Given P(t)=12+3.5t, find t if level p=26.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use an original function and check its rule, inverse, constraints, and units at multiple inputs.
Steps: State that the fitted trend is only supported within its stated t range.
WorkedExamples.Check: Forward and inverse values agree without real-world trend claims.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Calling inverse time a litre quantity
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Input and output units switch during inversion.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Label inverse input v in litres and output t in minutes.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Applying tank formula after it empties
Claiming a fitted model's inverse predicts real historical events precisely
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Regression/fit is approximate and only based on observed data.

SummaryPoints: Invert a function by expressing original input in terms of original output.
The tank inverse maps remaining litres to elapsed minutes.
W(13)=47.5 L, 5L corresponds to30min in the simple linear model.
Teacher verifies context and valid domain before using predictions.
